stories.headline: Many crews at life-threatening calls lack a paramedic
stories.body: An HSJ analysis found that in large parts of the country, three in 20 ambulances reaching patients with life-threatening emergencies have no paramedic on the crew.
stories.why: It feeds straight into the skill-mix debate and what the paramedic's role on a frontline crew should be.

stories.headline: 21 patients died after heatwave ambulance delays
stories.body: Board papers show 21 patients died after delayed responses from an ambulance service during June's heatwave, when serious calls spiked sharply.
stories.why: Surge planning for extreme weather is a patient safety issue, not just a performance one.

stories.headline: Essex handover delays 'like 291 ambulances off the road'
stories.body: An East of England Ambulance Service report says August's lost handover hours equalled 291 ambulances off the road. Broomfield's average handover rose from about 26 minutes to over 1 hour 12 minutes. NHS England now wants a 45-minute maximum.
stories.why: Every hour held at hospital is an hour a crew can't respond to the next 999 call.

stories.headline: Welsh Ambulance overtime bill tops £109m
stories.body: FOI figures show staff worked nearly 3.9 million paid overtime hours since 2017, costing over £109m. The trust also had the highest sickness absence rate in NHS Wales, 7.7%, in April to June 2026.
stories.why: Heavy overtime and high sickness point to a stretched workforce, a key factor in wellbeing and retention.

stories.headline: SWASFT handles more than 7,000 incidents in a weekend
stories.body: South Western Ambulance Service responded to 3,502 incidents on Saturday and 3,535 on Sunday, around 10% above expected. It blamed seasonal illness, colder weather and hospital handover delays.
stories.why: Winter pressure has arrived early, with Bonfire Night still to come.
